observations: This is the third stats-snapshot consumer in the 0x5ef8000..0x5efb000 family (#3082 maps 0x5efda00, #3133 maps 0x5ef8360). It shares the helpers fmt_pct, map_find_insert and map_insert with #3133, but differs in three ways: it does NOT clear the map first, it computes secs with floating-point division instead of the integer divide-by-1e6 magic, and its chain walk tests five links instead of three or four.

The decimal conversion is inline here (the digit-count dispatch, the divide-by-100 magic and the pair table are all inlined in the consumer), while the sibling consumers call the standalone to_string helper 0x5d4f970 for the same job. The inlined copy uses the same table chunks and the same magic constants.

The nine counter names are RocksDB db.* property names plus the composed write-buffer-manager-limit-stops; the sibling 21-entry pair map is the RocksDB compaction-stats column header table. Both tables are built by one static initializer and both are global; only the 9-entry map is read by this routine.
The walker's RELATIVE relocation at 0x64ecf80 is the slot the chain walk compares against; the walker itself is never called directly anywhere in the binary.

owner_layout.+0x00..+0x40: nine u64 counters, one per registry key 0..8, read in registry order
owner_layout.+0x780: handler chain head pointer; links at +0x20 strides, slot at +0x98
owner_layout.+0x790: last timestamp (u64); subtracted from the chosen slot return

pair_table.built_by: same initializer 0x5efbd80: 21 {int, string, string} entries (stride 0x48) pair_range_inserted via 0x5ef0ea0 (count 21, first = -0x1900(%rbp))
pair_table.note: RocksDB-style compaction-stats column headers (short name, display name). This routine does NOT read the pair map; it is recorded for context because the same initializer builds it in the same stack region.

phase_1_counters.insert_or_assign: map_find_insert 0x5ef40a0 (std::map::operator[], site 0x5ef9a5f) returns &node+0x40, then the decimal string is move-assigned into it (inlined string move-assign)
phase_1_counters.loop: i = 0..8 in ebx; r12 advances 8 per iteration; owner counter at +8*i
phase_1_counters.name_lookup: global_int_map.at(i) (inlined lower_bound on the map at 0x65039c8; on a miss __throw_out_of_range("map::at") from the literal at 0x4408a7, site 0x5ef9dd6)

chain_walk.head: *(owner+0x780); links at +0x20 strides; slot at +0x98
chain_walk.rule: call the first link whose +0x98 slot differs from the walker; if the first four links all carry the walker slot, call the fifth link's slot

secs.division: secs = diff / 1e6, double divisor at 0x4599a0 verified = 1000000.0; note the sibling consumers #3082/#3133 compute secs with an integer divide-by-1e6 magic instead -- same result for diffs < 2**53, different rounding above it
secs.format: fmt_pct 0x5eec680 formats "%f" (literal at 0x432165, site 0x5ef9b9c; second arg global at 0x64ed730, file qword 0, never read by the helper per #3133)
secs.to_double: non-negative as signed: plain cvtsi2sd; negative as signed (js at 0x5ef9b6a): the standard fixup at 0x5ef9ef1, t = (v >> 1) | (v & 1), convert, double. The fixup is exact only for v >= 2**63, which is exactly its branch domain.

phase_3_uptime.assign: string_move_assign 0x5eebb20(&node+0x40, &fmt_string) (site 0x5ef9c6d); both stack strings are then disposed; the routine returns
phase_3_uptime.lookup: lower_bound on the ctx map with that key (root *(ctx+0x10), header ctx+0x08); string_compare 0x5eeb970 (three-way: memcmp over the shorter length, then the length difference clamped to the int range via the 0x80000000 bound; site 0x5ef9c59)

registry.built_by: static initializer 0x5efbd80..0x5effdbb (FDE, 3035 objdump lines), which builds a 9-entry {int, string} stack array (stride 0x28, slots -0x1900 + k*0x28) and range-inserts it via range_insert 0x5ef11e0 (count 9, first = -0x1900(%rbp), site 0x5efcad3).
